cot_history.reasoning_cot: Day 1: no opponent trace, so bid based on supply scarcity and my hp. Subsequent days: exploit yesterday's max bid: if high (opponent desperate), bid lower if I'm healthy, else match. Keep budget for future.
Exploit Cindy's aggressive bidding from yesterday (avg 135). With supply unknown, bid 60% of salary when supply high (>20), else 85% to outbid her conservatively. Use int() for indices.

Exploit opponent traces: Cindy bid 160.5 avg 135.4, others low. I will bid just above their highest recent bid if affordable, else bid conservatively to survive. Use previous_trace to react dynamically.

Cindy and David survived with high bids. To secure water in medium supply, bid aggressively based on scarcity and urgency. Use yesterday's highest opponent bid as a benchmark, adding a margin if needed, while preserving budget for future days.

Will exploit yesterday's bid from opponents. If any opponent bid very high (>120), they may be desperate and low on HP, so we can bid lower. If we are low on HP, bid aggressively. Otherwise, bid around 55-60% of salary to stay competitive.

Opponents show varying aggression: Alex spent nearly all budget, Bob/David conserved. Use yesterday's trace bids to adjust: if opponents were aggressive, bid cautiously when healthy; if desperate, match. Supply influences base bid.

Opponents Alex and Cindy bid very high (avg 98-122). Eric needs to survive by bidding enough to win, but avoid overspending. Use previous_trace highest bid as reference. Opponents show extreme variance: Bob bids very high (avg 99), David moderate (avg 36). To win, avoid bidding wars early; outbid only when necessary. Use previous day's highest bid to decide: if high, bid aggressively if low HP; otherwise bid slightly above moderate. Conserve budget for later.
